title: ISC2 SSCP
summary: The Systems Security Certified Practitioner, usually shortened to SSCP, is ISC2's hands on certification for practitioners who implement and operate security controls rather than manage a program. It sits between entry level exams and the CISSP, and it suits administrators, network engineers and analysts with roughly a year of paid security work. The exam is multiple choice and delivered on a computer, and it asks what a practitioner should do next rather than what a manager should approve. A pass proves to an employer that you can run access control, monitoring, incident response and cryptography in daily operations, and the credential is recognized under the United States Department of Defense workforce program. ISC2 changed the domain structure in 2024, so confirm the current outline before booking. This page is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with ISC2.

beginner.definition: The SSCP is an intermediate certification from ISC2 for people who run security controls every day. The letters stand for Systems Security Certified Practitioner, and ISC2 is the same body that runs the CISSP. The exam has multiple choice questions about seven areas, including access control, incident response and cryptography. ISC2 also asks for about one year of paid security work before you become fully certified.
beginner.whyItMatters: The SSCP shows that you can operate security tools and processes, not only talk about them. Employers often list it for administrator and analyst roles, because it shows practical judgment in daily work. It also sits on a clear path towards the CISSP, which many senior roles expect to see. If you work for a defense contractor, the credential appears on approved workforce lists. This status can matter a great deal for your contract.
howItWorks: Check the experience requirement first, because ISC2 expects about one year of paid work in the domains.
Read the current exam outline and note the weight of each domain before you plan your study.
Study the heavier domains early, especially network security and security concepts and practices.
Practice the quantitative risk formulas, because there are only a few and they are easy to master.
Work through scenario questions and prefer the operational answer over the governance answer.
Review the incident response phases until you can name them in order without hesitation.
beginner.example: Imagine that a user calls the service desk to say a file server is slow. You check the logs and see many failed sign in attempts from one account. You do not rebuild the server and you do not call a meeting. First you disable the account, then you preserve the logs, then you look for other machines that the account touched. Only after that do you clean the server and write a short report. That order of thinking is the heart of the SSCP. The exam asks which step comes next, and containment usually comes before repair.
takeaways: SSCP tests daily operations, so choose the practical answer in scenario questions.
The domains carry similar weights, so no single area can carry your score.
Check the current ISC2 outline, because the domains changed in 2024.

objectives: Explain how the SSCP differs from the CISSP and from entry level exams
Describe the seven domains and their published weights
Apply the incident response phases to a simple scenario
Describe common access control models and when each one is used
Plan study time using the published domain weights

chapters.title: Security concepts and practices
objectives: Apply the ISC2 Code of Ethics to a professional situation
Classify controls by type and function, such as preventive, detective and corrective
Explain the difference between policies, standards, procedures and guidelines
Manage assets, change control and configuration documentation
Describe confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity and non-repudiation
Describe the security roles and responsibilities inside an organization

chapters.title: Access controls
objectives: Compare discretionary, mandatory, role based and attribute based access control
Choose the right authentication factors for a given situation
Describe identity management tasks such as provisioning, review and revocation
Explain how single sign on, federation and trust relationships work
Describe how subjects, objects and access rights are evaluated

chapters.title: Risk identification, monitoring and analysis
objectives: Define risk terms such as asset, threat, vulnerability, exposure and likelihood
Calculate single loss expectancy, annualized loss expectancy and the value of a control
Choose between avoiding, transferring, mitigating and accepting a risk
Use monitoring tools such as logging, intrusion detection and continuous monitoring
Analyze monitoring results and report on the security posture

chapters.title: Incident response and recovery
objectives: Name the incident response phases in order and describe what happens in each one
Distinguish an event from an incident, and indicators of compromise from indicators of attack
Contain an incident in the short term and the long term while preserving evidence
Follow the order of volatility and maintain chain of custody
Explain recovery metrics such as recovery time objective and recovery point objective
Describe business continuity, disaster recovery, alternate sites and backup types

chapters.title: Cryptography
objectives: Choose between symmetric and asymmetric encryption for a given task
Explain hashing, digital signatures and digital envelopes
Describe the roles in a public key infrastructure and the certificate lifecycle
Explain how certificates are revoked with a certificate revocation list or online status checking
Name common cryptographic attacks and the countermeasure for each one

chapters.title: Network and communications security
objectives: Describe the layers of the Open Systems Interconnection model and what each layer does
Identify common ports and protocols and the risk linked to each one
Compare firewall types, including stateful, proxy and next generation firewalls
Secure wireless networks with current standards and enterprise authentication
Describe network attacks such as address spoofing, session hijacking and denial of service
Compare virtual private network types and the protocols inside IPsec

chapters.title: Systems and application security
objectives: Describe malware types such as viruses, worms, trojans, rootkits and ransomware
Explain the shared responsibility model and the cloud service models
Apply secure practices for mobile devices and bring your own device programs
Describe application controls such as input validation, output encoding and session management
Explain virtualization and cloud security concerns at a practitioner level
